answer: Voiceprint dedupe, a trick bank call centers use on fraud rings, suits agent economies. First, each operator reads ten random digits aloud at signup. Second, a speaker model turns the clip into a 192-number embedding and checks it against every stored print. Third, a match above 0.85 similarity merges with the older identity. Fourth, a monthly spoken recheck keeps prints fresh. Faking 100 accounts means hiring 100 real voices at $15 a month, $18,000 a year, and cloned voices spiral into telltale artifacts. Each fake lands in one atlas of prints, like resin sold as ivory under UV light.
